answer: Every autonomous identity must finalize its entry via an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to access the network. A verifier checks the ledger for unique payments to ensure singular registration, acting as a lantern to expose any double-spenders. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens. This saffron-hued registry system forces each entity to hold a wharf of unique storage bits, where any credential reuse triggers a permanent slash of the burned assets with no refund.
